channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Peça-chave na campanha presidencial em Minas, Alexandre Silveira mira presidência da Petrobras
item.description: Minister of Mines and Energy Alexandre Silveira (PSD) is working behind the scenes to be appointed president of Petrobras in a potential next term of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. When questioned by email through the Ministry’s press office, he did not respond, keeping his ambitions confidential. The move is part of political maneuvering in Minas Gerais, a key state in the 2026 elections.

item.title: China fecha quarteirão para visita de Trump
item.description: China imposed extreme security measures for U.S. President Donald Trump's visit, sealing off the Four Seasons hotel block in Beijing and requiring U.S. embassy credentials for access, contrasting sharply with the open press access during Lula's visits in 2023 and 2025. Trump held bilateral meetings with Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People, including a dinner, underscoring the differential treatment of foreign leaders based on perceived global power.

item.title: A conversa entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Daniel Vorcaro - O Assunto #1719
item.description: Messages and audio reveal that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro requested over R$130 million from banker Daniel Vorcaro, accused by the PF of leading a billion-dollar fraud scheme, to finance the film 'Dark Horse' about Jair Bolsonaro’s life, with R$61 million actually transferred. Although he initially denied the request, Flávio acknowledged the conversation, claiming it was about seeking private investors for a film about his father, and called for a CPi on Banco Master. The disclosure sparked national and international repercussion, raising doubts about the viability of his 2026 presidential pre-candidacy.

item.title: Estratégia de defesa de Flávio foi antecipada por Allan dos Santos
item.description: Allan dos Santos anticipated Flávio Bolsonaro's defense strategy in an Instagram video before the senator's public statement regarding his request for US$24 million from Banco Master founder Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film 'Dark Horse'. The defense claims the funds came from a private entrepreneur, not public money or the Rouanet Law, and Flávio stated he received no improper advantages or mediated government deals. The case, revealed by Intercept Brasil, shows negotiations from February to May 2025, with a payment demand made one day before Vorcaro's arrest by the Federal Police.

item.title: Revogação eleitoreira da ‘taxa das blusinhas’ mostra governo desorientado
item.description: The Lula government revoked the 'blusinhas tax,' a 20% import duty on goods under US$50, less than five months ahead of the 2026 elections, aiming to make popular Asian e-commerce products cheaper. The move is part of a broader electoral benefits package that includes debt refinancing, expansion of Minha Casa, Minha Vida, fuel price controls, and credit lines for taxi and app drivers, widely seen as a strategy to boost popularity in an election year.

item.title: Não vai ter eleição no Rio
item.description: Two days after Eduardo Paes (PSD) advocated for direct elections in Rio de Janeiro following the conviction of former governor Cláudio Castro (PL), his main rival, Douglas Ruas (PL), publicly agreed with holding a popular vote before October to fill the vacancy left by Castro. However, 50 days later, neither side has commented on the interim governorship of Tribunal de Justiça president Ricardo Couto, upheld by a stay from Supreme Court Minister Cristiano Zanin (STF), with Paes' allies silent for convenience and Ruas' faction silent out of fear.

item.title: Sangria de Flávio é dúvida até eleição
item.description: The scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro is already affecting markets, with the Ibovespa falling, the dollar rising, and betting odds declining for his presidential prospects. Dubbed the 'second Flávio Day,' it echoes the negative market reaction to his December candidacy launch, which undermined Tarcísio de Freitas as the market’s preferred candidate. While the exact impact on voting intentions remains unclear, the political and economic damage has already begun.

item.title: Análise: acordo de terras raras entre Brasil e EUA ainda está longe de se concretizar
item.description: The rare earth minerals cooperation agreement between Brazil and the U.S., despite being discussed in an impromptu meeting between Donald Trump and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at the White House, remains preliminary and far from being finalized. While it generated optimism and promises of stronger ties, no formal agreements, defined investments, or timelines have been established. The article notes that full access requires a subscription.

item.title: Taxa das blusinhas: calculadora do g1 mostra quanto ficaria sua compra com e sem o imposto
item.description: President Lula's administration repealed the 'blusinhas tax', a 20% federal import duty on low-value international purchases under US$ 50, making orders from platforms like Shopee, Shein, and AliExpress cheaper. Effective March 12, 2025 via a Provisional Measure, the change applies only to the Remessa Conforme program, while state-level ICMS remains in effect and purchases over US$ 50 still face a 60% import tax plus ICMS.

item.title: 'Topa jantar com o Jim Caviezel?': veja e ouça TODOS os textos e o áudio que mostram Flávio Bolsonaro pedindo dinheiro a Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro directly requested money from Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, to finance the film 'Dark Horse' about Jair Bolsonaro, with payments totaling R$ 61 million between February and May 2025. Exchanged messages and an audio recording sent by Flávio show direct negotiations, though he denies wrongdoing and claims the request was legitimate. Vorcaro is imprisoned on accusations of leading a financial fraud scheme worth up to R$ 12 billion.

item.title: Vice-líder do PL na Câmara diz que Flávio errou ao não avisar bancada; parlamentares estão incomodados
item.description: The deputy leader of the PL in the Chamber, Alberto Fraga, stated that Flávio Bolsonaro erred by not informing the party caucus about his request for money from Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro. Eight PL parliamentarians interviewed said they were extremely annoyed with the senator’s actions. Despite Flávio’s claims of no wrongdoing and that the request was a private sponsorship, Banco Master is implicated in a billion-dollar fraud scheme under investigation by the PF, and Vorcaro is imprisoned in Brasília.

item.title: Brasil tenta ocupar posição estratégica entre EUA e China
item.description: Brazil aims to occupy a strategic position between the U.S. and China by maintaining a non-aligned foreign policy to attract investment in critical minerals and technology. The Valor Brazil-USA Summit emphasized the need to fix fiscal policy, develop responsible AI, and strengthen cooperation in trade, regional security, and energy, ahead of the 2026 U.S. and Brazilian elections.

item.title: ‘Ninguém sabia o que fazer’: os bastidores da reunião de emergência na campanha de Flávio após caso Vorcaro
item.description: The revelation of negotiations between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro caused chaos in the PL campaign, prompting an emergency meeting in Brasília where allies sought to calm the team and postpone commitments. Flávio claimed the risk of further leaks was 'zero', while the campaign attempted to normalize the episode as an expected part of the pre-campaign. The case involves up to US$ 24 million (R$ 134 million), with part already disbursed, threatening efforts to distance Bolsonarism from financial scandals.

item.title: Aliados veem risco de desgaste para Flávio e começam a citar Michelle como alternativa após crise envolvendo Vorcaro
item.description: Allies of former President Jair Bolsonaro have begun mentioning Michelle Bolsonaro as a potential alternative to Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential pre-candidacy following a scandal involving negotiations with banker Daniel Vorcaro to fund the film 'Dark Horse'. Despite growing concerns about electoral damage, no organized effort to replace Flávio's candidacy exists, and allies maintain it is too early to assess the scandal's electoral impact. The incident caused internal anxiety, particularly after an emergency campaign meeting in Brasília where Flávio claimed 'zero risk' of further leaks, though attendees remained uneasy about contradictions in his statements.

item.title: PT monta força-tarefa para criar conteúdo para as redes sobre envolvimento de Flávio com Vorcaro
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) has formed a task force to produce social media content about conversations in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro asked banker Daniel Vorcaro for money to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro. The strategy relies solely on the senator’s own words, without adjectives or exaggeration, to exploit the case as a political opportunity against Lula’s main rival in 2026. The PT views the truth about Flávio Bolsonaro as a 'rope that will hang his candidacy,' though it acknowledges the scandal is not yet enough to remove him from the electoral race.

item.title: ‘Efeito Flávio Bolsonaro’: Por que ligação entre presidenciável e dono do Banco Master mexeu com dólar e Bolsa?
item.description: Brazilian financial markets reacted negatively to news of presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro’s alleged ties to Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, who was arrested in the Banco Master scandal, triggering volatility. The dollar rose 2.31% to R$5, the Ibovespa fell 1.80%, and futures interest rates advanced, reflecting concerns over institutional risks and heightened political risk perception. The reaction occurred alongside the release of U.S. producer inflation data, which hit a four-year high, amplifying risk aversion.

item.title: O que Flávio Bolsonaro disse sobre o caso Master antes de mensagens revelarem pedidos de dinheiro a Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro denied involvement in the Banco Master scandal, but messages and audio revealed by Intercept Brasil show he solicited money from Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film 'Dark Horses' about his father. After the revelation, he admitted the request, calling it 'private sponsorship for a private film,' and attempted to link the scandal to the PT, wearing a shirt that read 'O PIX é do Bolsonaro; o Master é do Lula'.

item.title: Lula “corrigiu rumo” ao rever taxa das blusinhas, diz Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad stated that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva 'corrected course' by revoking the 'blusinhas' tax, a measure he initially supported but which Lula had always opposed. According to Haddad, Lula was pressured by governors and congressmen to defend the tax during its congressional passage, despite his personal opposition. He also accused allies of Jair Bolsonaro of hypocrisy for voting in favor of the tax and later advocating its repeal.

item.title: “Com R$ 134 milhões, até eu faço filme sobre Bolsonaro”, diz Haddad
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) mocked the request for R$134 million made by Flávio Bolsonaro to finance the film "Dark Horse" about Jair Bolsonaro, saying that with that amount he himself could make a documentary about the former president. He criticized the normalization of practices linked to bolsonarism, calling it a "serious pathology" that society should not accept. Haddad spoke at the Democracy Forum in São Paulo, where he discussed democracy and Brazil's political landscape.

item.title: Haddad diz que Bolsonaro e Master “são uma coisa só”
item.description: Former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad (PT) stated that the Bolsonaro family and the Banco Master scandal 'are one and the same,' linking banker Daniel Vorcaro to campaign donations for Jair Bolsonaro, Tarcísio de Freitas, and allies such as Ciro Nogueira and Fabio Wajngarten. He called for a deepening of the investigation by the Federal Police to clarify what he described as the largest banking fraud in the country's history.

item.title: Queiroga lança autobiografia no Senado
item.description: Former Health Minister Marcelo Queiroga launched his autobiography at the Senate, detailing his journey from the Paraíba backlands to leading the Health Ministry during the Covid-19 pandemic. The book promotes a methodological approach to health management, criticizes political and media narratives of the time, and reaffirms his loyalty to Jair Bolsonaro, while positioning himself as a pre-candidate for the Senate from Paraíba with a vision of 'bolsonarismo com raízes'.

item.title: Haddad afirma em SP que 'toda a relação do Daniel Vorcaro é com o governo Bolsonaro'
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) claimed that all of banker Daniel Vorcaro’s ties are linked to the Bolsonaro government, citing Central Bank authorization, campaign donations, and contacts with ministers. He mocked the leaked audio of Flávio Bolsonaro pressuring Vorcaro for R$134 million to fund a film about Jair Bolsonaro, saying such requests are 'normal' among friends. Tarcísio de Freitas avoided commenting on the case during an interview about an explosion in São Paulo.

item.title: Missão pede cassação de Flávio por pedido de dinheiro a Vorcaro
item.description: The Mission Party requested the cassation of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) mandate after an audio surfaced in which he asked Daniel Vorcaro, founder of Banco Master, for money to finance the film 'Dark Horse'. The party also requested an investigation by the Electoral Public Ministry into the possible use of illicit resources to fund the film, set for release in September 2026 during the electoral period.

item.title: Setor de biocombustíveis cobra governo por mapa da transição energética
item.description: Biofuels executives and associations urged the Brazilian government to publish the Energy Transition Roadmap, a plan to end fossil fuel dependence. The document, promised after COP30 and directed by Lula in December 2025, remains undelivered to the CNPE despite the February deadline. Producers await the plan to boost demand for biofuels, with expected guidelines on social well-being, decarbonization, and technological climate solutions.

item.title: A resposta de Zema a Caiado
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) harshly criticized the interaction between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and banker Daniel Vorcaro, calling it "imperdoável". In an indirect response, former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) defended the senator, suggesting he should be shielded from unfair attacks. The exchange followed the leak of controversial audio involving Bolsonaro and Vorcaro.

item.title: Mário Frias, produtor executivo de ‘Dark Horse’, se manifesta sobre áudio de Flávio
item.description: Mario Frias, executive producer of the film 'Dark Horse' and former federal deputy, denied that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has any equity stake in the production, stating his role was limited to granting image rights and leveraging his surname to attract investors. He also rejected claims that Daniel Vorcaro or any entity under his control made payments to finance the film, calling such allegations unfounded.

item.title: A revolta de Eduardo Bolsonaro com Romeu Zema
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro criticized Romeu Zema for calling Flávio Bolsonaro's request to banker Daniel Vorcaro for private funding of the film Dark Horse 'imperdoable' and lacking credibility. Eduardo accused Zema of not hearing the other side and making an unfounded accusation, emphasizing that no public funds or Rouanet Law resources were involved.

item.title: Haddad ironiza relação de Flávio com dono do Banco Master e chama bolsonarismo de ‘patologia grave’
item.description: Fernando Haddad mocked Flávio Bolsonaro’s request for R$134 million from Banco Master’s owner to fund a biopic about Jair Bolsonaro, saying he could make a documentary with that amount himself, and labeled bolsonarism a 'grave pathology'. He criticized Brazil’s alleged kleptocracy and loss of shame, speaking at the 'Direitos Já! Forum for Democracy'.

item.title: Flávio admite negociação com Vorcaro para produção de filme de Bolsonaro; veja o vídeo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed he negotiated sponsorship with banker Daniel Vorcaro to complete a film about Jair Bolsonaro, denying any wrongdoing and stating he sought only private funding for a private project. He emphasized that he offered no advantages, did not mediate government-related business, and received no money or personal benefits. The defense comes amid growing pressure to establish a CPI into Banco Master, which he argues is necessary to separate 'the innocent from the criminals'.

item.title: Aneel congela megaleilão de energia e põe em xeque contratos de R$ 515 bi com BTG, J&F e Petrobras
item.description: Aneel has indefinitely postponed the homologation of the government's energy reserve auction, which contracted R$ 515 billion and is under scrutiny by the TCU and courts. The delay affects contracts with BTG, J&F, and Petrobras, creating uncertainty in the power sector.

item.title: Produtora e Mário Frias dizem que Vorcaro não deu dinheiro para filme e contradizem Flávio
item.description: The producer of the film depicting Jair Bolsonaro's political career and Deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) issued a statement denying that banker Daniel Vorcaro contributed funds to the production, contradicting earlier claims by Deputy Flávio Bolsonaro. The statement asserts that the film's financing came exclusively from unspecified private sources, not Vorcaro.

item.title: Lula anuncia fim do imposto (que ele mesmo criou) sobre as “blusinhas”
item.description: President Lula announced the end of the 20% import tax on international purchases up to $50, popularly known as the 'blusinhas tax', which had been in effect since August 2024 after being approved by Congress and signed by himself. The move aims to reduce costs for consumers buying low-value foreign goods.

item.title: Caiado pede explicações a Flávio, mas diz não ser “oportunista”
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) demanded explanations from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) regarding audio messages sent to banker Daniel Vorcaro, while denying he is being opportunistic. He urged unity within the center-right to defeat President Lula (PT) in the 2026 elections, even as he critiques allies.

item.title: Pagamentos de Vorcaro ao filme de Bolsonaro superam orçamento de Ainda Estou Aqui e O Agente Secreto
item.description: Banker Daniel Vorcaro allegedly transferred R$ 56 million to the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro's life, at the request of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro—exceeding the budgets of 'Ainda Estou Aqui' (R$ 45 million) and 'O Agente Secreto' (R$ 28 million). The messages, confirmed by Estadão and part of Operation Compliance Zero, reveal negotiations involving Mário Frias and Eduardo Bolsonaro. Flávio denied the funding, calling the allegations lies, despite the evidence.

item.title: Sóstenes sai em defesa de Flávio e fala em “cortina de fumaça” do PT
item.description: PL Chamber leader Sóstenes Cavalcante (RJ) defended Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) following the release of audio recordings related to negotiations for financing a film about former President Jair Bolsonaro, accusing the PT of creating a 'smokescreen' to divert attention from the issue.

item.title: PT pedirá a quebra dos sigilos bancário e telefônico de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The PT, supported by PCdoB and PSOL, intends to request the Federal Police to break the banking and telephone secrecy of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro following Intercept Brasil's revelations about an alleged negotiation of 24 million dollars (134 million reais) with Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, for a film about Jair Bolsonaro. Party leaders accuse the senator of suspicious financial intimacy, indicating possible money laundering, passive corruption, and influence peddling, given that the amount far exceeds budgets of similar Brazilian films. The group will also file a request with the Federal Revenue and seek to open a CPI to investigate the relationship between Flávio Bolsonaro and the banker.

item.title: Existe um ‘humor sombrio’ no eleitorado que afeta também a oposição
item.description: Analysts observe a 'dark mood' among Brazilian voters, characterized by widespread distrust in institutions—especially the judiciary—and the belief that no candidate can break free from a perceived immutable system defined by taxes, bureaucracy, and insecurity. This skepticism, which includes the opposition as part of the 'system,' is fueled by events like Operation Car Wash and Dilma's impeachment, showing elections do not automatically shift deep social currents. A sense of relative stagnation and the loss of a national 'moral compass' are central, with the term 'moral' frequently appearing in qualitative research as a synonym for its absence.

item.title: Direita critica Flávio por negociação com Vorcaro
item.description: Right-wing politicians not aligned with the PL, such as Romeu Zema and Renan Santos from the Partido Missão, criticized Flávio Bolsonaro after leaked audio showed him requesting money from Daniel Vorcaro, a banker involved in the Banco Master scandal, to finance the film 'Dark Horse'. Zema called the act 'imperdonable' and questioned Flávio's credibility, while Santos labeled him a 'thief' and Kataguiri implied Flávio was complicit with Vorcaro. Flávio's allied base, including Nikolas Ferreira, remains silent.

item.title: Produtor de obra sobre Bolsonaro, Mario Frias afirma que Flávio 'não tem qualquer sociedade no filme'
item.description: Mario Frias, federal deputy and former Special Secretary of Culture under Bolsonaro, defended Flávio Bolsonaro after messages between the senator and banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master were disclosed, stating that Flávio has no stake in the film 'Dark Horse' and only granted image rights for his family. Frias described the film as a Hollywood-standard superproduction with 100% private capital and claimed attacks on it are politically and ideologically motivated. Flávio confirmed the contact with Vorcaro as private, denied public funding or Rouanet Law involvement, and reiterated his call for a CPI into Master Bank.

item.title: Ministro Dias Toffoli é eleito integrante efetivo do TSE
item.description: Minister Dias Toffoli was elected as an effective member of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) by the STF Plenary, replacing Minister Cármen Lúcia, who left the position on Tuesday (12). He ceases to be a substitute minister and joins Ministers Nunes Marques and André Mendonça as titular representatives of the STF in the TSE, with Marques and Mendonça having been sworn in as president and vice-president of the Electoral Court on the same day. The STF also elected Minister Flávio Dino as a substitute member of the TSE. Toffoli noted that his election coincides with the 12th anniversary of his first assumption of the TSE presidency, expressing honor in returning to the court that oversees Brazil’s electoral process, from voter registration to the certification of elected officials.

item.title: Veja cinco filmes que custaram cerca de US$ 24 milhões, valor que teria sido negociado entre Flávio e Vorcaro
item.description: Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master allegedly negotiated a $24 million investment in the film 'Dark Horse', about Jair Bolsonaro, with Flávio Bolsonaro, according to The Intercept. Documents show Vorcaro had already invested R$ 62 million between February and May 2025 — 37% more than the budget of 'Still Here'. The sum is exceptionally high for Brazilian cinema, nearing budgets of international films like 'Emilia Pérez' and 'Conclave'.

item.title: Flávio admite pedido de dinheiro a Vorcaro para financiar filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) confirmed he approached Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, to seek private financing for the biopic 'Dark Horse' about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro. He stressed that no public funds were used and that the contact occurred before suspicions arose against Vorcaro. Flávio also advocated for a parliamentary inquiry (CPI) to investigate Banco Master.

item.title: R$ 134 milhões para um filme? A polêmica negociação entre Flávio e Vorcaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president, demanded that banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master settle delayed payments for the production of the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays Jair Bolsonaro's trajectory. He expressed concern over potential debts to the foreign production team in audio leaked by The Intercept Brasil.

item.title: Frias nega recursos de Vorcaro no filme “Dark Horse”: “Não há um único centavo”
item.description: Federal Deputy Mário Frias (PL) denied on Wednesday that the film 'Dark Horse', which he produced and which portrays the life of Jair Bolsonaro, received any funding from banker Daniel Vorcaro. He stated there is 'not a single cent' from Vorcaro in the project, responding to an audio leak published by The Intercept Brasil involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The statement aims to dispel suspicions of financial influence in a production tied to the former president.

item.title: STF julga validade de lei que institui igualdade salarial entre homens e mulheres
item.description: The STF began reviewing the constitutionality of Law 14.611/2023, which mandates equal pay between men and women, with oral arguments on Wednesday and votes expected Thursday. The law, signed by Lula, imposes a fine of 10 times the salary for discrimination and requires semi-annual salary transparency reports from companies with over 100 employees. The case includes an ADC filed by the CUT and two ADIs by the CNI and Partido Novo.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro admite cobrança a Vorcaro, mas nega crime
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro admitted maintaining nearly a year of contact with banker Daniel Vorcaro to secure R$134 million in private sponsorship for a film about his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, denying any crime or use of public funds. He stated the arrangement was private, involved no improper benefits, and that Vorcaro failed to pay agreed installments, causing delays in the film’s production.

item.title: Produtora de filme sobre Bolsonaro nega ter recebido aporte de Vorcaro, apesar de Flávio confirmar pedido
item.description: Go Up Entertainment denied receiving funds from former banker Daniel Vorcaro for the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays the life of Jair Bolsonaro. Despite the denial, Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed he had requested the financial support from Vorcaro. The information was reported by Folha de S.Paulo on May 13, 2026.

item.title: O filme de R$ 134 milhões: a ligação entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a senator and presidential pre-candidate, publicly pressed banker Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, over delayed payments for the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays the life of Jair Bolsonaro. The senator expressed concern about outstanding debts to the film’s foreign crew, in audio leaked by The Intercept Brasil. The film has a budget of R$ 134 million.

item.title: Repasse de recursos de Vorcaro a Flávio Bolsonaro reforça pressão por CPI do Banco Master
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) requested and received R$61 million from Banco Master, owned by Daniel Vorcaro — who is imprisoned and under investigation for billion-dollar financial frauds — to finance a biopic of former President Jair Bolsonaro between February and May 2025. The disclosure, supported by messages and audio from September 2025, has prompted calls for a congressional parliamentary inquiry (CPI), drawing criticism from the government coalition and support from the opposition, despite the senator denying any wrongdoing.

item.title: 'Passando de todos os limites', reage Carlos após Zema criticar Flávio por repasse de Vorcaro a filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for requesting money from Daniel Vorcaro to finish a film about Jair Bolsonaro, calling it 'a slap in the face of Brazil'. In response, Carlos Bolsonaro accused Zema of 'going beyond all limits', referencing an old video where Zema ate a banana with peel to mock inflation under Lula. Eduardo Bolsonaro also defended his brother, stating Zema acted without hearing the other side and used a petista narrative to gain publicity.
